assertion: K.S.A. 45-218(d) requires a response within three business days; K.S.A. 45-219 limits fees to actual cost.
record: To be measured. Capture for each target: days to response, fee quoted, exemption cited, and whether the exemption matches the records withheld.
source_doc: KORA request copies and agency responses
generalizes_how: This is already the design of the KORA matrix. The harvest addition is to log each divergence as a numbered finding rather than only as a tracker row, so that individual refusals become citable.
charitable_reading: Agencies commonly miss the three-day window for volume reasons rather than to obstruct.
next_action: Add a finding_id column cross-reference to the KORA response tracker

assertion: Agency ALPR policies state retention periods, access controls, and audit-log requirements.
record: To be measured. Compare each agency's stated policy against the audit logs, retention settings, and sharing agreements actually produced in response to a records request.
source_doc: Agency ALPR policy; audit logs; interagency sharing agreements
generalizes_how: Policy-versus-practice comparison runs identically for any surveillance technology with a written policy and a machine-generated log. The instrument is technology-agnostic.
charitable_reading: A gap between written policy and vendor default configuration is frequently an oversight at procurement rather than a deliberate practice.
reform_hook: Statutory retention limits and mandatory audit-log disclosure for ALPR
est_scale: Every ALPR-operating agency in the state
next_action: Confirm the audit-log request language captures logs rather than policy only

assertion: RSMo 610.100 provides access to mobile video recordings, and agency retention schedules for such recordings are commonly short.
record: An indigent misdemeanor defendant is typically not appointed counsel until the initial appearance, commonly around three weeks after the incident. Where an agency's retention period for mobile video is thirty days, the preservation window can expire at or near the moment counsel first appears.
source_doc: RSMo 610.100; agency retention schedules; published median arrest-to-appointment intervals
generalizes_how: Collect, for a set of agencies, the mobile-video retention period, and for a set of courts, the median interval from arrest to appointment of counsel. Where the first number is smaller than the second, the statutory right of access is structurally unavailable to indigent defendants.
charitable_reading: Retention periods are set by storage cost and by schedules that predate widespread body-worn camera use; the interaction may simply never have been considered.
reform_hook: Automatic preservation on arrest; extended retention where charges are filed; earlier appointment of counsel
est_scale: Statewide; every indigent misdemeanor defendant in a recorded encounter
next_action: Request retention schedules as public records -- they are not case-specific and can be obtained now

assertion: Section 600.042.4(2) RSMo (eff. Aug. 28, 2024) and 18 CSR 10-2.010(1)(B) condition public defender representation in a misdemeanor case on the charge being one which "will probably result in confinement in the county jail upon conviction," unless the prosecuting or circuit attorney has waived a jail sentence.
record: To be measured. Neither the statute nor the regulation names who makes the confinement determination, sets a standard of proof for it, requires that it be made before eligibility is decided, or requires that it appear on the record. The practical effect to be tested is whether eligibility is denied on a determination that no judicial officer has made, and whether the denial is ever revisited before sentencing.
source_doc: Section 600.042.4(2) and 4(6) RSMo; 18 CSR 10-2.010(1)(B); MSPD eligibility determination letters; circuit court dockets
generalizes_how: For a set of Missouri circuits, collect misdemeanor cases in which appointed counsel was denied on the no-confinement ground. Measure three numbers: the share whose docket contains any judicial confinement determination at all; the share whose eventual disposition is a suspended imposition or suspended execution of sentence, or probation; and the share of those later revoked to county jail. Where denial routinely precedes any judicial determination, the gate is operated without the finding it presupposes. Where uncounseled dispositions carry suspended jail terms, compare against Alabama v. Shelton, 535 U.S. 654 (2002), which holds that a suspended sentence that may end in actual deprivation of liberty may not be imposed on an uncounseled defendant. The same instrument runs in any state whose appointment standard turns on predicted confinement rather than authorized confinement.
charitable_reading: The standard is predictive, and at the application stage no one yet knows the sentencing posture. The defender office is the party holding the caseload data to predict it, and the prosecutor's jail waiver resolves a large share of cases without anyone needing to decide. A determination made late rather than early may reflect sequencing rather than avoidance.
reform_hook: Section 600.042.4(2) RSMo -- assign the confinement determination to the court, require it on the record before eligibility is denied, and require re-determination before any suspended jail sentence is imposed on an uncounseled defendant
est_scale: Statewide; every misdemeanor application denied on the no-confinement ground
next_action: Request aggregate counts -- not case files -- from MSPD and a sample of circuit clerks: no-confinement eligibility denials per year, and disposition codes for those cases
